title: Ex-Britain First leader arrested in HMO attacks investigation

input.lead: Ashlea Simon says she was arrested at Manchester Airport in connection with her identifying HMOs
input.summary: Ashlea Simon says she was arrested at Manchester Airport in connection with her identifying HMOs
input.evidence_text: Ex-Britain First leader arrested in HMO attacks investigation - BBC News Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Ashlea Simon said she was arrested after her social media posts visiting HMOs in Salford By Charlotte Hall Local Democracy Reporting Service Published 27 October 2026 The former co-leader of the far-right Britain First party has said she was arrested as part of an investigation into attacks on houses in multiple occupation (HMOs). In a post on X, Ashlea Simon said she had been held at Manchester Airport after "returning from a family holiday". Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said a 37-year-old woman had been arrested on suspicion of "conspiracy to cause criminal damage", following a spate of incidents in which HMOs were vandalised across the Greater Manchester region. Simon, who said in her post that she "hasn't committed a crime in her life", was approached for comment by the Local Democracy Reporting Service (LDRS). In the post, Simon said she believed the arrest was linked to a series of videos she has made since July. In them, she claimed to identify several HMOs in her hometown of Walkden, Salford. In a previous video shared by Simon in recent days, she said police had "raided" her home while she was on holiday and she was aware of an "arrest warrant". Simon left Britain First two years ago, and is now the leader of a "pro-English" activism group. The news of her arrest came amid a major investigation into a number of vandalism attacks across Salford, Tameside, and Stockport. Police are investigating about 50 incidents in which HMOs and family homes have been vandalised and cars targeted. In one incident, a pig's head was left outside a home. input.lead: Traffic England says queues stretched eight miles (13km) following the crash at about 03:30 GMT
input.summary: Traffic England says queues stretched eight miles (13km) following the crash at about 03:30 GMT
input.evidence_text: Five injured in M6 crash as motorway remains partially closed - BBC News Image source, Highways England Image caption, The collision on the northbound M6 in Cheshire caused lengthy delays By Angela Ferguson North West Published 27 October 2026 Five people have been injured in a crash involving a van and a car that resulted in the closure of a motorway in both directions, causing severe delays. Cheshire Police said the collision happened at about 03:30 GMT on the northbound M6 at junction 20 near Warrington, where it meets the M56 at Lymm Interchange. A North West Ambulance Service spokesperson said five people had been taken to hospital, two of whom with serious injuries. The traffic monitoring service Inrix said both carriageways had since reopened. Traffic England said vehicles had been diverted off the M6 via the exit and entry slip roads and later reported delays of 90 minutes, with tailbacks stretching eight miles (13km). Inrix said southbound traffic had built up to junction 22 for Newton-le-Willows, while those heading northbound queued back towards junction 18 for Middlewich and Holmes Chapel. A serious illness, the loss of a loved one, or something unexpected affecting your ability to work can turn life upside down overnight. Would you know what to do next? This is what I often refer to as a "lifeboat moment" – when normal life stops and you're forced to navigate a completely different reality Planning for a lifeboat moment means having some really difficult conversations. What would happen if you weren't around? If your income stopped tomorrow? If you had to manage the finances on your own? For many, the biggest challenges are surprisingly practical. input.evidence_text: Litter and leaves swept up by new investment – Bolton Council Published: Tuesday, 27th Oct 2026 Streets in Bolton are set to be cleaner after the council invested in new equipment to tackle litter, leaves and fly-tipping. New road sweepers have been purchased, bigger bins installed at key spots and handy equipment stores provided for volunteer litter pickers. A fleet of road sweepers in various sizes are used by the council to remove leaves and litter, and there have been several recent additions. One large sweeper has been added, making three in total, and these are vital for keeping roads and drains clear of leaves and twigs in autumn, which reduces the risk of flooding as well as keeping streets looking tidy. Six smaller mechanical sweepers are used on pavements, with teams focusing on different areas of Bolton on a rotating schedule. A new electrically powered pavement sweeper has also been brought in that can get into smaller spaces like cycle lanes, helping to keep them clean and safe to use. The sweepers are among the equipment used by Environmental Services teams who spent the summer doing things like cutting grass and spraying weeds, and who have now switched to autumn jobs like gathering leaves. They target routes such as Chorley New Road and Gilnow Road that have lots of trees and remove the leaves and detritus they produce. Bigger roads are also benefiting from new, larger litter bins as part of a major programme of improvements on Bolton’s main transport routes. Almost 50 bins have been replaced with ones that have more than twice the capacity, meaning they are less likely to get full and cause litter to overflow onto the street. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. A £300,000 restoration, long-term lease and 23-year-old head chef are shaping what comes next Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been serving Manchester since 1867, but owner Roger Ward admits there was a point after Covid when he wasn’t sure how much longer he wanted to keep doing it Tom’s had gone eight years without a proper lease and much longer without any meaningful investment by the landlord. input.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained.
